title: Don't lose the volts in the leads
story: Your bench supply is set to 5.00 V. A board that behaves like a 10 ohm resistor (about half an ampere) needs at least 4.9 V at its own pins. Choose the two test leads: one from the supply's plus terminal to the board, one from the board back to minus. Each lead is shown as its resistance.

goals.label: the board gets at least 4.9 V
the board gets no more than 5 V

hints: Both leads and the board are in series: I = 5 / (10 + R_lead1 + R_lead2).
The board gets 5 * 10 / (10 + R_leads). For 4.9 V the two leads together may have at most about 0.2 ohm.
One bad lead is enough to fail: the same current flows through both.
